DERIVED from the only disclosed absolute figures. USA Rare Earth's 20 Apr 2026 investor deck gives 2027E separated-oxide output of 164 t Dy and 29 t Tb; footnote 3 states 'Assumes 95% recovery yield from MREC to separated oxides', so contained in MREC is (164 + 29) / 0.95 = 203 t. The merger proxy records 150 t TREO produced in 2024 and only 40 t in 2025, and the COO told Bloomberg in Apr 2026 that Pela Ema 'now produces roughly 100 metric tons of rare earth oxides each year'. At ~100 tpa TREO the contained Dy+Tb today is about 4 t, roughly 2% of the figure recorded here. Serra Verde is a ramp-stage asset; do not give this number a 'currently flowing' weighting in disruption ranking. CORROBORATION from an independent document: Mineracao Serra Verde's own 2015 pilot assay (CETEM) puts Dy2O3 at 3.23% and Tb4O7 at 0.53% of product TREO, which against the 6,400 tpa LOM TREO average implies Dy 207 / Tb 34 = 241 t contained - 16% above the 2027E figure, consistent with 2027 being a ramp year rather than LOM steady state. Two further checks pass: La at 32% of TREO reproduces USAR's stated '~4,400 tpa after Lanthanum removal' from 6,400 tpa, and the 2015 mass basket priced at the proxy's own 2028E deck reproduces projected 2028E revenue to within ~6%. description: Ionic-clay operation in Goias, Brazil, and the subject of USA Rare Earth's pending US$2.83bn acquisition. Phase I is expected to average approximately 6,400 t/yr TREO contained in MREC over life of mine, with commercial operations expected in 2027 - as at 31 Dec 2025 the proxy states 'the Project remains in the development stage and has not yet achieved the milestones necessary to be considered operational', which contradicts the earlier claim held here that it has been in production since 2024. Financed by a DFC facility of up to US$565 million (initial tranche up to US$465m plus a second tranche up to US$100m), of which approximately US$325 million was outstanding at 31 Mar 2026. A 15-year 100% offtake with per-element floor prices to US SIIE, LLC was signed 20 Apr 2026. TWO EVIDENCE GAPS: no per-element Dy/Tb tonnage or grade split appears anywhere in the proxy, and there is no S-K 1300-compliant resource or reserve - 'A qualified person has not done sufficient work to classify these estimates as current estimates of mineral resources or mineral reserves'. One is promised in the first 10-K after closing. THE OFFTAKE IS NOW LIVE AND THE LOCK IS NARROWER THAN IT LOOKS. US SIIE, LLC is identified by the U.S. Department of War as a special purpose vehicle it capitalised with US$750 million through the IBAS programme, inside a US$1.55 billion structure that also carries a US$300 million Defense Logistics Agency purchase commitment and a US$500 million money-center bank commitment. Conditions precedent were satisfied 21-24 Aug 2026 and the agreement is 'now in force and in full effect', with first deliveries expected early Q4 2026. SCOPE IS 100% OF PHASE 1 Nd, Pr, Dy AND Tb ONLY, take-or-pay - but YTTRIUM IS EXPRESSLY CARVED OUT and is 42% of life-of-mine basket VALUE, and a potential Phase 2 of roughly +6,400 tpa TREO is not covered. So Serra Verde is locked for magnet rare earths and free for yttrium and any expansion. Floor prices: Tb US$2,050/kg, Dy US$575/kg, Nd and Pr US$110/kg, escalating 2% a year, with 70% of any excess over the market index returning to the seller - note these were struck BELOW then-prevailing ex-China spot, so they are downside insurance rather than a subsidy. Term is legally the earlier of 198 million tonnes of run-of-mine ore or 20 years from a Commercial Operations Date that has not yet occurred; the '15-year' framing used throughout USAR and Serra Verde marketing is not reconciled to that anywhere and should be treated as shorthand. US SIIE additionally holds a CALL OPTION OVER ALL SVRE EQUITY, triggered by events including breach of the change-of-control provisions - a sovereign lock on the asset, not just the tonnes. Residual risk: the US$500m facility funding the SPV's purchases is an undocumented, unfunded commitment expiring 31 Dec 2026.

Two claims exist on Stage 1 concentrate: Iluka's binding 6,000 dmt/yr for 15 years (90,000 dmt total, containing 9,600 dmt NdPr), and approximately 12,500 tpa to Lindian's own SARECO plant in Kazakhstan - 18,500 tpa in total. Lindian materially managed this: it TERMINATED the Gerald Metals SPA on 19 Jun 2026, which had held roughly 40% of Stage 1, explicitly to 'allow for the earlier supply of product to the SARECO hydromet facility in Kazakhstan'. TWO ILUKA ROFR TRIGGERS ARE ARGUABLY LIVE: expansion 'beyond its initial capacity of up to 18,000dmt per annum' would oblige Lindian to offer Iluka 33% or 80% of incremental production up to 31,000 dmt/yr, and 18,500 tpa crosses that threshold; and Iluka holds a further ROFR where Lindian sells 'on less favourable terms' than Iluka's - which makes transfer pricing to a now wholly-owned SARECO a live question. value.note: LOWER BOUND, NOT A PRODUCTION FIGURE - Mt Weld discloses no production at all. Derived by mass balance from a MEASURED downstream actual: Lynas Malaysia produced 62 t of Dy+Tb across FY26 (9 t Q1, 26 t Q2, 8 t Q3, 19 t Q4, src-lynas-q4-fy26-quarterly). Lynas Malaysia's only feed is Kalgoorlie and Kalgoorlie's only feed is Mt Weld, so every tonne separated in Malaysia was contained in Mt Weld concentrate; beneficiation and separation recoveries are below 100%, so contained Dy+Tb at the mine is >= 62 t. UPPER BOUND ~300 t, also disclosed: Lynas states its 250 t Dy / 50 t Tb nameplate is 'subject to sourcing other potential feedstock', which is the operator's own statement that Mt Weld alone cannot fill it. Use 62-300 tpa as the range; the lower bound is what ranking needs. DO NOT substitute the reserve-grade route (0.63% Dy2O3 + 0.16% Tb4O7 = 0.79% of TREO, 5 Aug 2024 reserve): that is an ORE-basis ratio and the Mt Weld CONCENTRATE assemblage is a hard null across all 1,767 Lynas ASX announcements, so flotation fractionation is unquantified. It does give a free consistency check - inverting 62 t at 0.79% implies roughly 7,850 t TREO through the chain, which should be reconciled against Lynas's FY26 REO production. This is the only Dy/Tb feed figure in the graph derived from material that actually moved.

description: Ionic-clay rare earth project in northern Tasmania. value.note: PFS BASIS, PARTLY SUPERSEDED - TREAT AS AN UPPER BOUND. 'Annual Production (REO) 9,448 t' from PFS Table 3, contained TREO in the MREC product over a 20-year LOM on 5 Mtpa of ore at 3,380 ppm TREO feed and 57% TREO recovery. NOT separated oxide. The August 2026 DFS revised the mine plan - MREO fell from 3,518 to 2,967 tpa (-16%) on the same 5 Mtpa throughput over a 25-year life - so the DFS TREO figure is almost certainly lower than 9,448, but no DFS TREO number appears in anything read here. Replace this entry when the primary DFS is anchored.

Contained NdPr in the MREC product, NOT separated NdPr oxide. Recorded so the Dy+Tb subtraction on this node is auditable in the data rather than only in prose: 2,967 tpa MREO minus this 2,843 tpa NdPr is the 124 tpa mat-dytb-combined entry. SECONDARY - quoted by news.metal.com from the DFS announcement; the primary has not been read. The PFS equivalent was 36% of 9,448 t = about 3,401 tpa.

DERIVED, NOT DISCLOSED - Viridis never states a Dy+Tb tonnage. The derivation is a DEFINITIONAL SUBTRACTION, not a basket assumption: Viridis defines MREO as Dy2O3 + Nd2O3 + Pr6O11 + Tb4O7 (PFS footnote B, primary and read), so MREO minus NdPr is exactly Dy2O3 + Tb4O7. On the August 2026 DFS figures, 2,967 tpa MREO minus 2,843 tpa NdPr = 124 tpa. CONTAINED IN MREC, NOT SEPARATED OXIDE. FOUR INDEPENDENT ROUTES CONVERGE ON 117-142 tpa: (1) the DFS subtraction above = 124; (2) the same subtraction on PFS Table 3 - MREO 3,518 minus 36% of 9,448 t TREO (3,401) = 117, though 36% is rounded to a whole percent so this route alone carries roughly +/-70 t; (3) the PFS's own MREC assemblage, Dy2O3 + Tb4O7 = 1.5% of product TREO in the Northern Concessions and 1.3% in the Southern Complex (Tables 6 and 7), which on 9,448 tpa TREO gives 123-142 t; (4) sister deposit Caldeira, the same Pocos de Caldas alkaline complex at comparable scale, discloses 127 tpa. CONFIDENCE IS MEDIUM DESPITE THE CONVERGENCE, and the reason is the source, not the arithmetic: both DFS inputs are quoted from secondary outlets (MREO 2,967 from mining.com.au, NdPr 2,843 from news.metal.com) and the primary DFS announcement has not been read. Anchor src-viridis-colossus-dfs-2026 and this number can move to REPORTED. REJECT ON SIGHT - 190 tpa: the PFS's own page 2 headline says '9,500 tonnes of TREO and 3,500 tonnes of MREO, with a high-value mix comprising 36% NdPr oxides and 2% DyTb oxides', and 2% of 9,500 is 190. That is contradicted by Tables 3, 6 and 7 of the SAME DOCUMENT, which put Dy+Tb at 1.2-1.5% of TREO. The 2% is a rounded-up headline; the tables are the claim. REJECT ON SIGHT - roughly 380 tpa: obtained by applying the ~4%-of-TREO Dy+Tb share that holds for Serra Verde (3.8%) and Makuutu (4.44%) to a 9,500 tpa TREO output. It is about 3x too high because Pocos de Caldas clays are lanthanum-dominated (La2O3 44-48% of product TREO) and Dy+Tb is only 1.3-1.5% here. 'Ionic clay' is not a basket - the parent lithology is. NO PER-ELEMENT SPLIT IS RECORDED. The PFS does disclose Dy2O3 and Tb4O7 separately, but only to one decimal place (1.2%/0.3% and 1.1%/0.2%), so the implied Dy:Tb of 4.0-5.5 spans 3.6-7.7 once rounding is carried through. Splitting an INFERRED combined figure with a ratio that coarse would compound two estimates - the same reason Mountain Pass's 120 t own-feed entry is left unsplit. Note that the pooled median of 5.92 must NOT be used here: Caldeira's disclosed 4.64 in the same complex is the correct comparator, and it sits below the graph's ionic-clay band.

description: The largest undeveloped ion-adsorption clay rare earth resource outside China, and the closest thing in this graph to a fully funded ex-China ionic clay mine: DFS complete (20 Aug 2026), US$449M total pre-production capital, equity requirement of about US$135M fully covered by about US$150M of identified sources, FID targeted Q4 2026 and first production H2 2028. An MREC Demonstration Plant is already running in Brazil and reported July 2026 MREO recoveries of 78.1% against DFS assumptions of 76-78%. Debt is advanced but not closed - Goldman Sachs and Cutfield Freeman mandated, letters of support from Export Finance Australia (up to US$50M), Export Development Canada (up to US$100M), Bpifrance and a BNDES/FINEP joint support plan, with lender term sheets targeted end-September 2026. WHY IT MATTERS HERE, AND WHY LESS THAN ITS SIZE SUGGESTS: Colossus is a big project with a small Dy/Tb number. At roughly 124 tpa contained Dy+Tb it ranks around ninth of the fifteen quantified mines in this graph, below Caldeira and barely above Donald, because the Pocos de Caldas basket is lanthanum-dominated and Dy+Tb is only 1.3-1.5% of product TREO. It is an NdPr project that carries heavies, not a heavies project. THE OFFTAKE IS THE OPEN QUESTION: the 20 Aug 2026 funding release lists 'finalising binding offtake' as an immediate priority and names NO separation counterparty, so the SUPPLIES edge is UNRESOLVED. Colossus is therefore ex-China mine supply with no committed ex-China separation home - the same structural position as Serra Verde, Fingerboards, Lofdal and Makuutu, and the reason the aggregate 'refining nameplate versus mine feed' comparison understates how much unattached feed exists. CAVEAT ON EVERY DFS NUMBER ON THIS NODE: the DFS results announcement itself has not been read - it is identified by exact title and date from Reference 3 of the funding release, but the figures came from secondary outlets.
